docs.title: minimal_mjx
docs.text:
Starter code for MJX-based reinforcement learning from the Dynamic Mobility Lab. It is built on MuJoCo Playground and Brax PPO. It keeps training, checkpointing and evaluating policies simple.

The example Cheetah policy after 50M environment steps (about 8 minutes of training).

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A swappable backend. Write an environment once. Run it on JAX/MJX (jnp) for fast parallel training, or on NumPy and the C MuJoCo bindings (np) for fast, debuggable rollouts.
  • A base environment class, SwappableBase, with common reward terms and helpers.
  • A config-agnostic library. Library functions take plain arguments (run_dir, ppo_params, network_params, ...). Config is the only code that knows the YAML layout, so you can use your own layout by subclassing it, or skip it entirely.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install minimal_mjx            # from PyPI
pip install -e ".[dev]"            # from source, with pytest

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
From the repository root:

# Train the example Cheetah into example/results/cheetah/test/
python -m example.train   --config example/cheetah.yaml --no_wandb

# Roll out the latest checkpoint and save a video and reward plot
python -m example.rollout --config example/cheetah.yaml

docs.title: Building these docs
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme. The API reference is generated from docstrings by mkdocstrings.

pip install -e ".[docs]"
mkdocs serve           # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict  # what CI runs; fails on broken links and references

The configuration lives in mkdocs.yml at the repository root, and the pages in docs/:

docs/
├── index.md              # home page
├── examples/             # step-by-step walkthroughs of example/*.py
├── guides/               # the config file, writing an environment
├── api/                  # one page per subpackage, generated from docstrings
├── developer.md          # this page
└── assets/               # plots and videos shown on the site

.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site on every pull request and publishes it to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

docs.title: Writing docstrings
docs.text:
The API pages pick up every public function, class and method automatically: a new function appears as soon as it exists in a module the reference covers. Underscored names are left out. Docstrings use the Google style:

def load_policy(run_dir, deterministic=True, checkpoint_path=None):
    """Load a policy from a checkpoint.

    Args:
        run_dir: Run directory to take the newest checkpoint from.
        deterministic: If True, the policy returns the mean action.
        checkpoint_path: A specific checkpoint to load instead.

    Returns:
        A function ``(obs, rng) -> (action, extras)``.
    """

To link to an API entry from any page, use its full path as a Markdown reference: [`train`][minimal_mjx.learning.training.train].

A new module needs a minimal_mjx.<subpackage>.<module> line on its subpackage's page in docs/api/.

docs.title: Keeping the examples in sync
docs.text:
The step-by-step pages quote excerpts of example/train.py and example/rollout.py. The full listing at the bottom of each page is included straight from the file, so it never goes stale, but the excerpts and their explanations need updating by hand when the scripts change.

The plot and video in docs/assets/ come from the run in example/results/cheetah/test. To refresh them after a new run:

ffmpeg -i example/results/cheetah/test/rollout.mp4 -vf "scale=540:540,fps=50" \
    -c:v libx264 -crf 28 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart -an docs/assets/cheetah-rollout.mp4
ffmpeg -ss 4 -i docs/assets/cheetah-rollout.mp4 -frames:v 1 docs/assets/cheetah-rollout-poster.jpg

class SwappableBase(mjx_env.MjxEnv):
    """Atalante walker task."""

    def __init__(self,
            xml_path: Path,
            env_params: config_dict.ConfigDict,
            backend = 'jnp',
            num_free = 3
        ):
        """Initializes the base "swappable" MJX environment for RL training and 
        evaluation. This class implements core functionalities that are common 
        among various roboics tasks. Moreover, this class 
        implements a swappable backend for JAX and NumPy, allowing for 
        flexibility when it comes to training and evaluation (i.e. JaX for
        training and NumPy for evaluation).

        Args:
            xml_path: Path to the XML file defining the robot and environment.
            config: Configuration dictionary for the environment.
            config_overrides: Optional dictionary to override specific config values.
            backend: Backend to use for computations, either 'jnp' for JAX or 'np' for NumPy.
        """
        super().__init__(env_params)
        self.params = env_params
        self._xml_path = xml_path.as_posix()

        self._spec = mj.MjSpec.from_file(
            filename=self._xml_path, 
            assets=common.get_assets()
        )
        self._mj_model: mj.MjModel = self._spec.compile()
        self._mj_model.opt.timestep = self.params.sim_dt
        self._mj_model.opt.timestep = self.sim_dt

        self.setup_swappable_backend(backend)

        self.nq = self._mj_model.nq
        self.nv = self._mj_model.nv
        self.nu = self._mj_model.nu
        self.qpos_free = num_free
        self.qvel_free = num_free - 1 if num_free == 7 else num_free

        self._jt_lims = self._mj_model.jnt_range[num_free:].T

    def setup_swappable_backend(self, backend: str):
        """Sets up the backend for the environment."""
        self.backend = backend
        if backend == 'jnp':
            # Setup JAX backend
            self._np = jnp
            self._mj = mjx
            self._uniform = jax.random.uniform
            self._normal = jax.random.normal
            self._bernoulli = jax.random.bernoulli
            self._split = jax.random.split
            self._splice = jax.lax.dynamic_slice
            self._cond = lambda cond, true_fn, false_fn, operand: jax.lax.cond(
                cond, true_fn, false_fn, operand
            )
            self._mjx_model = mjx.put_model(self._mj_model)

            self._step_fn = lambda data, ctrl, model=self._mjx_model: mjx_env.step(
                model, data, ctrl, self.n_substeps
            )

            def mjx_data_init_fn(qpos, qvel, ctrl, time, xfrc_applied, model=self._mjx_model) -> mjx.Data:
                data = mjx.make_data(model).replace(
                    qpos=qpos, qvel=qvel, ctrl=ctrl, time=time, xfrc_applied=xfrc_applied
                )
                data = mjx.forward(model, data)
                return data.replace(ctrl=ctrl)

            self._data_init_fn = mjx_data_init_fn

            self._state_init_fn = lambda data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info: mjx_env.State(
                data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info
            )

            self._set_val_fn = lambda arr, val, min_idx=None, max_idx=None: arr.at[min_idx:max_idx].set(val)

            self._set_xfrc_fn = lambda data, xfrc_applied: data.replace(xfrc_applied=xfrc_applied)

            self._set_model_params_fn = lambda model, **kwargs: model.replace(
                **kwargs
            )

        elif backend == 'np':
            # Setup numpy backend
            self._np = np
            self._mj = mj
            self._uniform = lambda key, shape=None, minval=0.0, maxval=1.0: np.random.uniform(
                low=minval, high=maxval, size=shape
            )
            self._normal = lambda key, shape=None, loc=0.0, scale=1.0: np.random.normal(
                size=shape
            )
            self._mjx_model = self._mj_model
            self._split = lambda key, num=2: (None for _ in range(num))  # No RNG in np backend

            def splice(operand, start_indicies, slice_sizes):
                slices = tuple(slice(start, start + size) for start, size in zip(start_indicies, slice_sizes))
                return operand[slices]
            self._splice = splice

            def cond(cond, true_fn, false_fn, operand):
                if cond:
                    return true_fn(operand)
                else:
                    return false_fn(operand)
            self._cond = cond

            def init_data(time, qpos, qvel, ctrl, xfrc_applied, model):
                data = mj.MjData(model)
                data.time = time
                data.qpos = qpos
                data.qvel = qvel
                data.ctrl = ctrl
                data.xfrc_applied = xfrc_applied
                mj.mj_forward(model, data)
                data.ctrl = ctrl

                return data
            self._data_init_fn = lambda time, qpos, qvel, ctrl, xfrc_applied, model=self._mj_model: init_data(
                time, qpos, qvel, ctrl, xfrc_applied, model
            )

            def mj_step(model, old_data, ctrl, n_substeps):
                new_data = mj.MjData(model)

                # Allocate state buffer
                state_size = mj.mj_stateSize(model, mj.mjtState.mjSTATE_FULLPHYSICS)
                state = np.empty(state_size)

                # Copy state from old_data
                mj.mj_getState(model, old_data, state, mj.mjtState.mjSTATE_FULLPHYSICS)

                # Set state in new_data
                mj.mj_setState(model, new_data, state, mj.mjtState.mjSTATE_FULLPHYSICS)

                # Step simulation
                for _ in range(n_substeps):
                    new_data.ctrl[:] = ctrl
                    mj.mj_step(model, new_data)

                return new_data
            self._step_fn = lambda data, ctrl, model=self._mj_model, n_substeps=self.n_substeps: mj_step(
                model, data, ctrl, n_substeps
            )

            self._state_init_fn = lambda data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info: EnvState(
                data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info
            )
            def set_val(arr, val, min_idx=None, max_idx=None):
                copy_arr = arr.copy()
                copy_arr[min_idx:max_idx] = val
                return copy_arr
            self._set_val_fn = set_val

            def set_xfrc(data, xfrc_applied):
                data.xfrc_applied = xfrc_applied
                return data
            self._set_xfrc_fn = set_xfrc

            def set_model_params(mj_model, **kwargs):
                for key in kwargs:
                    setattr(mj_model, key, kwargs[key])                

                return mj_model

            self._set_model_params_fn = lambda model, **kwargs: set_model_params(
                model, **kwargs
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported backend: {backend}")

    def add_random_joint_state(
        self,
        jt_key: jax.Array,
        qpos: jax.Array,
        minval: jax.Array,
        maxval: jax.Array,
    ):
        # TODO: This does not appropriately handle joints with no limits
        val = self._uniform(jt_key, qpos[self.qpos_free:].shape[0], minval=minval, maxval=maxval)
        val = self._np.clip(val + qpos[self.qpos_free:], *self._jt_lims)
        qpos = self._set_val_fn(qpos, val, min_idx=self.qpos_free, max_idx=None)
        return qpos

    @abstractmethod
    def reset(self, rng: jax.Array) -> mjx_env.State:
        """Resets the environment to an initial state. Takes in a random key
        (rng) as input and outputs the initial state of the environment."""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    @abstractmethod
    def step(self, state: mjx_env.State, action: jax.Array) -> mjx_env.State:
        """Steps the environment with an action outputted by the policy network.
        This function is run after policy evaluations and returns an Markov Decision
        Process state, which includes the observation for the next policy evaluation."""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    @abstractmethod
    def reward_function(
        self, data: mjx.Data, action: jax.Array, info: dict, done: bool
    ):
        """Returns reward terms as a dictionary ({name: reward value}). These
        rewards are then summed in a weighted fashion based on their name and the
        weight values provided in your config."""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    @property
    def action_size(self):
        """Required action size for the environment"""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    @abstractmethod
    def _get_obs(self, data: mjx.Data, info: dict):
        """Returns the observation given the data and info."""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    @property
    def observation_size(self):
        if self._np == jnp:
            return super().observation_size
        else:
            abstract_state = self.reset(jax.random.PRNGKey(0))
            obs = abstract_state.obs
            if type(obs) == dict:
                return len(obs['state'])
            return obs.shape

    def make_history(self, data, length):
        history = self._np.repeat(
            data[self._np.newaxis, :],
            length,
            axis=0
        )
        return history

    def update_history(self, history, new_data):
        history = self._np.roll(history, shift=1, axis=0)
        return self._set_val_fn(history, new_data, max_idx=1)

    def get_metrics(
        self,
        metrics,
        rewards
    ):
        weights = self.params.reward.weights
        for k, v in rewards.items():
            metrics[f"reward/{k}"] = weights[k] * v

        return metrics

    def get_reward_and_metrics(
        self,
        rewards,
        metrics
    ) -> tuple[jax.Array, dict[str, jax.Array]]:
        _rewards = {k: v * self.params.reward.weights[k] for k, v in rewards.items()}
        reward = sum(_rewards.values())

        metrics = self.get_metrics(metrics, rewards)

        return reward, metrics

    # Generally useful rewards for RL....
    def reward_alive(self) -> jax.Array:
        """Reward for being alive."""
        return 1.0

    def reward_euclidean_imitation(
        self, qpos: jax.Array, reference: jax.Array, imitation_sigma: jax.Array
    ):
        """Reward for imitating. Can be applied to joints and flying frame."""
        deviation = self._np.linalg.norm(qpos - reference)
        error = self._np.square(deviation)
        return self.exp_reward(error, imitation_sigma)

    def reward_action_rate(
        self, act: jax.Array, last_act: jax.Array, last_last_act: jax.Array
    ):
        """Reward for the rate of change of the action"""
        c1 = self._np.sqrt(self._np.sum(self._np.square(act - last_act)))
        c2 = self._np.sqrt(self._np.sum(self._np.square(act - 2 * last_act + last_last_act)))
        return c1 + c2

    def reward_vector_size(
        self, v: jax.Array, size_sigma: jax.Array
    ) -> jax.Array:
        mag2 = self._np.sum(self._np.square(v))
        return self.exp_reward(mag2, size_sigma)

    def exp_reward(self, mag2: jax.Array, sigma: jax.Array):
        return self._np.exp(-mag2 / sigma)

    @property
    def xml_path(self) -> str:
        return self._xml_path

    @property
    def mj_model(self) -> mj.MjModel:
        return self._mj_model

    @property
    def mjx_model(self) -> mjx.Model:
        return self._mjx_model

    @property
    def spec(self) -> mj.MjSpec:
        return self._spec

def make_dummy_inference_fn(env: mm.envs.SwappableBase, mode='zero'):
    """Makes a 'fake' inference function for simulating the environment without 
    a policy. Modes are 'zero' (which sends all zeros as the action) and 
    'random' (which sends random actions in [-1, 1])"""
    inference_fn = None
    match mode:
        case 'zero':
            inference_fn = lambda obs, rng: (np.zeros(env.action_size), None)
        case 'random':
            inference_fn = lambda obs, rng, size=env.action_size: (2 * np.random.random(size) - 1, None)
        case _:
            raise Exception(f'Unknown inference type {mode}')

    return inference_fn

def rollout_policy(
    inference_fn,
    env           : MjxEnv,
    n_steps       = 100,
    info_init_fn  = lambda state: state.info,
    info_step_fn  = lambda state: state.info,
    info_plot_key = None,
    width         = None,
    height        = None,
    gen_vid       = True,
    show_progress = True,
    camera        = None,
) -> tuple[list, list, plotting.RewardPlotter, plotting.MujocoPlotter, plotting.InfoPlotter]:
    width, height = plotting.infer_frame_dim(env.mj_model, width, height)
    step, reset = mm.learning.inference.get_step_reset(env)

    # Set up the environment
    rng = jax.random.PRNGKey(np.random.randint(0, 100000))
    state: mm.EnvState = reset(rng)

    # Initialize the state
    initial_info = state.info | info_init_fn(state)
    state = state.replace(info=initial_info)

    # Setup reward plotting
    reward_plotter = plotting.RewardPlotter(state.metrics)
    data_plotter = plotting.MujocoPlotter()
    info_plotter = plotting.InfoPlotter(plotkey=info_plot_key)
    data_plotter.add_row(state.data)

    # Rollout and record data
    N = int(n_steps)
    traj = [state]
    for i in tqdm(range(N), disable=not show_progress):
        ctrl, _ = inference_fn(state.obs, rng)
        state = step(state, ctrl)
        state = state.replace(info=state.info | info_step_fn(state))
        data_plotter.add_row(state.data)
        reward_plotter.add_row(state.metrics, state.reward)
        info_plotter.add_row(state.data.time, state.info)
        traj.append(state)

        if state.done:
            break

    scene_option = plotting.get_mj_scene_option(contacts=False, com=False)

    if gen_vid:
        print('Generating video...')
        frames = env.render(
            trajectory   = traj,
            camera       = camera,
            height       = height,
            width        = width,
            scene_option = scene_option,
        )
    else:
        frames = None
    return frames, traj, reward_plotter, data_plotter, info_plotter

    """Open-loop policy that emits uniform random actions in ``[-1, 1]``."""

def make_sinusoidal_policy(
    action_size: int, amp: float = 0.8, freq: float = 1.5, phases=None, **kwargs
):
    """Open-loop sinusoid ``amp * sin(2*pi*freq*t + phases)``, identical across envs.
    """
    if phases is None:
        phases = jnp.zeros(action_size)
    else:
        phases = jnp.asarray(phases)

    def policy(obs, key, t):
        batch_shape = get_batch_shape(obs)
        action = amp * jnp.sin(2.0 * jnp.pi * freq * t + phases)  # (action_size,)
        return jnp.broadcast_to(action, (*batch_shape, action_size)), {}

    return policy

def make_open_loop_policy(policy_desc: str, action_size: int, **kwargs):
    """Build an open-loop policy by name (``'zero'``, ``'random'``, ``'sinusoid'``).

    Extra kwargs are forwarded to the underlying factory.

    if policy_desc not in OPEN_LOOP:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown open-loop policy '{policy_desc}'. Expected one of {list(OPEN_LOOP)}."
        )
    factory = OPEN_LOOP[policy_desc]
    return factory(action_size, **kwargs)

def setup_ppo(ppo_params: dict, network_params: dict, resumed: Resume | None = None):
    """Default handler: brax PPO. Returns ``(train_fn, network_factory)``.

    ``train_fn`` is a :func:`functools.partial` of the brax PPO trainer with all
    algorithm params pre-bound; ``network_factory`` builds the PPO networks.
    """
    network_factory = functools.partial(
        ppo_networks.make_ppo_networks,
        mean_kernel_init_fn=jax.nn.initializers.lecun_uniform,
        **network_params
    )
    train_fn = functools.partial(
        train_ppo, **ppo_params,
        network_factory=network_factory,
        # brax restores the checkpointed params and normalizer, not its optimizer.
        restore_checkpoint_path=None if resumed is None else str(resumed.path),
        wrap_env_fn=wrapper.wrap_for_brax_training,
    )
    return train_fn, network_factory

def find_resume(output_dir) -> Resume | None:
    """Where training left off in ``output_dir``, or None if it never checkpointed.

    The epoch count is the number of checkpoints past the one written at step 0, which is
    what a run writes per epoch; taking it from the directory keeps it right across
    several continuations, and across a schedule whose epochs changed size.
    """
    checkpoints = find_checkpoints(output_dir)
    if not checkpoints:
        return None
    return Resume(checkpoints[-1], int(checkpoints[-1].name), len(checkpoints) - 1)

def apply_resume(ppo_params: dict, resumed: Resume) -> dict:
    """A copy of ``ppo_params`` asking the algorithm for only the steps the run still owes.

    ``num_timesteps`` is the run's whole budget, so continuing a run is a matter of
    raising it: the algorithm is handed the difference.
    """
    total = ppo_params['num_timesteps']
    if resumed.step >= total:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{resumed.path.parent} has already trained {resumed.step} of the "
            f"{total} steps in num_timesteps; raise num_timesteps to continue it"
        )
    print(
        f'Resuming {resumed.path.parent} from {resumed.step} steps (epoch '
        f'{resumed.epoch}); {total - resumed.step} steps left of {total}'
    )
    return {**ppo_params, 'num_timesteps': total - resumed.step}

def create_training_directory(run_dir, overwrite=False, resume=False) -> Path:
    """Create the run output directory, refusing to clobber an earlier run.

    If the directory already exists but holds nothing a run produced -- only a stale
    config, or the run id of a job that died before its first epoch -- it is reused.
    ``overwrite`` reuses it whatever it holds (e.g. for scratch runs), and so does
    ``resume``, for a run that continues the checkpoints already there.
    """
    # Written before training starts, so their presence alone is not training output.
    stale = {'config.yaml', mm.utils.logging.RUN_ID_FNAME}
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    if run_dir.exists():
        if not (resume or overwrite) and not all(
            path.is_file() and path.name in stale for path in run_dir.iterdir()
        ):
            raise FileExistsError(f"Training directory already exists: {run_dir}")
    else:
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return run_dir

def train(
    env,
    eval_env,
    run_dir,
    train_fn_params,
    network_factory_params,
    handle_params,
    run=None,
    progress_cls=None,
    resume=False,
    overwrite=False,
):
    """Train a policy on the given environment.

    Creates ``run_dir``, resolves the training algorithm via ``handle_params``
    then wraps the resulting ``train_fn`` with progress/checkpoint callbacks and runs
    it. Saving the run's config is up to the caller (see
    :meth:`minimal_mjx.utils.config.Config.save`).

    Args:
        env: Training environment.
        eval_env: Evaluation environment used for periodic rollouts.
        run_dir: Directory for checkpoints and progress output.
        train_fn_params: Algorithmic parameters for your specific training algo.
        network_factory_params: Keyword arguments for the network factory.
        run: (optional) Experiment-tracking handle (e.g. a wandb run).
        handle_params: Callable
            ``(ppo_params, network_params, resumed) -> (train_fn, network_factory)``,
            where ``resumed`` is a :class:`Resume` or None.
        progress_cls: (optional) Progress callback class, built as
            ``progress_cls(save_dir, total_timesteps, run)`` and handed to the
            algorithm through its ``plot_progress`` method. Defaults to
            :class:`minimal_mjx.utils.plotting.Progress`.
        resume: (optional) If True, continue the checkpoints already in ``run_dir``
            instead of refusing to overwrite it. ``num_timesteps`` is then the run's
            total budget and the algorithm trains what is left of it, checkpointing
            and plotting on the step axis the earlier job stopped on. An algorithm opts
            in by reading ``resumed``; without that it retrains its whole share from
            scratch into the same directory.
        overwrite: (optional) If True, train into ``run_dir`` even if it holds an
            earlier run's output.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(make_inference_fn, trained_params, metrics)``.
    """
    if progress_cls is None:
        progress_cls = mm.utils.plotting.Progress
    output_dir = create_training_directory(run_dir, overwrite=overwrite, resume=resume)
    mm.utils.logging.save_run_id(output_dir, run)

    train_fn_params = dict(train_fn_params)
    total_timesteps = train_fn_params['num_timesteps']
    resumed = find_resume(output_dir) if resume else None
    if resume and resumed is None:
        print(f'Nothing to resume in {output_dir}; training from scratch.')
    if resumed is not None:
        train_fn_params = apply_resume(train_fn_params, resumed)
    # Steps the algorithm reports are its own; the run's axis carries on from here.
    step_offset = 0 if resumed is None else resumed.step

    # Resolve the training algorithm.
    train_fn, network_factory = handle_params(train_fn_params, network_factory_params, resumed)

    # PPO params are still read here for the network config and progress plot. The algo
    # was handed the steps still owed, but the plot reports against the whole budget.
    train_fn_params = {**train_fn_params, 'num_timesteps': total_timesteps}
    network_config = checkpoint.network_config(
        observation_size=eval_env.observation_size,
        action_size=eval_env.action_size,
        normalize_observations=train_fn_params['normalize_observations'],
        network_factory=network_factory,
    )

    def save_model_fn(current_step, make_policy, params, training_state=None):
        """Checkpoint the policy, and the learner state a continued run would need."""
        step = step_offset + current_step
        mm.utils.logging.save_model(
            step, make_policy, params,
            network_config = network_config,
            output_dir     = output_dir,
            run            = run,
        )
        if training_state is not None:
            mm.utils.logging.save_training_state(output_dir, step, training_state)

    progress = progress_cls(output_dir, total_timesteps, run)
    if resumed is not None:
        progress.load(before=resumed.step)
    times = progress.times
    first = len(times)  # this job's own rows, for the timings printed below
    train_fn = functools.partial(
        train_fn,
        progress_fn=lambda num_steps, metrics: progress.plot_progress(
            step_offset + num_steps, metrics
        ),
        policy_params_fn=save_model_fn,
    )

    print(
        'Started training at',
        datetime.now(ZoneInfo("America/New_York")).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z")
    )
    make_inference_fn, trained_params, metrics = train_fn(
        environment=env,
        eval_env=eval_env,
    )
    print(f"time to jit: {times[first + 1] - times[first]}")
    print(f"time to train: {times[-1] - times[first + 1]}")

    return make_inference_fn, trained_params, metrics

def get_all_models(run_dir: Path | str, sort: bool = True) -> List[Path]:
    """Return all checkpoint directories in ``run_dir``, sorted by step if requested."""
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    if not run_dir.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Model directory does not exist: {run_dir}")
    model_files = [
        path for path in map(Path, glob(str(run_dir / '*')))
        if path.is_dir() and path.name.isdigit()
    ]
    if sort:
        model_files.sort(key=lambda x: int(x.name))
    return model_files

class Config:
    """Reads a run's YAML config and hands its values to library functions.

    This is the only place that knows the YAML layout. Library functions take plain
    arguments (``run_dir``, ``ppo_params``, ...), so a different config layout only
    needs a subclass that overrides these properties.
    """

    def __init__(self, config: Path):
        self.cfg = read_config(config)

    def load(self, config):
        self.cfg = read_config(config)
        return self.cfg

    def save(self, path: Path = None, make_dir=True, rewrite_test=True, warn_github_changes=True):
        """Write the config to ``path`` (default ``run_dir / 'config.yaml'``).

        Runs not named ``test`` record the current git commit as ``git_hash``.
        """
        if path is None:
            path = self.run_dir / 'config.yaml'
        if make_dir:
            os.makedirs(self.run_dir, exist_ok=self.is_test)

        if not self.is_test and rewrite_test:
            self.cfg.git_hash = get_commit_hash(warn=warn_github_changes)

        save_config(self.cfg, path)

    @property
    def algorithm(self) -> str:
        """Learning algorithm, e.g. ``'ppo'`` (the default when unset)."""
        return self.cfg.get('algorithm', 'ppo')

    @property
    def env_name(self) -> str:
        """Environment class name, e.g. ``'Cheetah'``."""
        return self.cfg.env

    @property
    def backend(self) -> str:
        """Backend for evaluation environments, ``'np'`` or ``'jnp'``."""
        return self.cfg.backend

    @property
    def env_params(self) -> config_dict.ConfigDict:
        """The ``env_config`` section, given to env classes as ``env_params``."""
        return create_config_dict(self.cfg.env_config.to_dict())

    @property
    def ppo_params(self) -> dict:
        """Brax PPO settings, passed to the trainer as keyword arguments."""
        return self.cfg.learning_params.ppo_params.to_dict()

    @property
    def network_params(self) -> dict:
        """Network settings for the configured algorithm."""
        return self.cfg.learning_params.network_params.to_dict()

    @property
    def normalize_observations(self) -> bool:
        """Whether training keeps a running observation normalizer."""
        return self.cfg.learning_params.ppo_params.normalize_observations

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """Run name."""
        return self.cfg.name

    @name.setter
    def name(self, value: str):
        self.cfg.name = str(value)

    @property
    def is_test(self) -> bool:
        """Runs named ``test`` may be overwritten and do not record a git hash."""
        return self.name == 'test'

    @property
    def save_dir(self) -> Path:
        """Parent directory of all runs for this config."""
        return Path(self.cfg.save_dir)

    @save_dir.setter
    def save_dir(self, value):
        self.cfg.save_dir = str(value)

    @property
    def run_dir(self) -> Path:
        """Run directory: ``save_dir / name``."""
        return self.save_dir / self.name

def flatten_config(config, parent_key='', sep='/'):
    """Flatten a nested (dict-like) config so every leaf is keyed by its path, joined by `sep`.
    """
    items = {}
    for key, value in config.items():
        key = str(key)
        if sep in key:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Config key '{key}'{f' (under {parent_key})' if parent_key else ''} contains "
                f"'{sep}', which is reserved as the delimiter between nesting levels. Rename "
                f"the key (e.g. '{key.replace(sep, '_')}') or flatten with a different `sep`."
            )
        new_key = f'{parent_key}{sep}{key}' if parent_key else key
        if hasattr(value, 'items'):
            items.update(flatten_config(value, new_key, sep=sep))
        else:
            items[new_key] = value
    return items

def unflatten_config(flat_config, sep='/'):
    """Inverse of `flatten_config`: rebuild a nested config from its `a/b/c` keys.
    """
    config = {}
    for key, value in flat_config.items():
        if key.startswith('_'):
            continue
        *parents, leaf = key.split(sep)
        node = config
        for depth, parent in enumerate(parents):
            node = node.setdefault(parent, {})
            if not isinstance(node, dict):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cannot unflatten '{key}': '{sep.join(parents[:depth + 1])}' is a "
                    f"value ({node!r}), not a section."
                )
        node[leaf] = value
    return config

def get_latest_artifact(run: wandb.apis.public.Run, prefix: str) -> wandb.Artifact:
    """Return the last-logged artifact of `run` whose name contains `prefix`, or raise ValueError."""
    matches = [artifact for artifact in run.logged_artifacts() if prefix in artifact.name]

            f"No '{prefix}' artifact found for run {run.id}. "
            f"Logged artifacts: {[a.name for a in run.logged_artifacts()] or 'none'}"
        )
    return matches[-1]

    run: wandb.apis.public.Run, prefix: str, iterations: float
) -> wandb.Artifact:
    """Return the first artifact of `run` matching `prefix` written at or past
    `iterations` training steps, or raise ValueError.

    A checkpoint artifact records the step it was written at in `metadata['iteration']`,
    so the choice is made from the run's artifact listing without downloading any of them.
    """
    matches = [
        artifact for artifact in run.logged_artifacts()
        if prefix in artifact.name and 'iteration' in artifact.metadata
    ]
    past = [a for a in matches if a.metadata['iteration'] >= iterations]
    if not past:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No '{prefix}' artifact at or past {iterations:.0f} iterations for run "
            f"{run.id}. Logged iterations: "
            f"{sorted(a.metadata['iteration'] for a in matches) or 'none'}"
        )
    return min(past, key=lambda a: a.metadata['iteration'])

def download_model(run_id: str, run_dir: Path | str,
                   entity: str, project: str, prefix: str,
                   iterations: float | None = None) -> str:
    """Download a W&B run's config and a policy checkpoint into ``run_dir``.

    The config is saved, unchanged, as ``run_dir / 'config.yaml'`` (rebuilt from the
    run's logged config if it has no config artifact). Its paths still point at where
    the run trained, so update them before reusing it, e.g. with
    :class:`minimal_mjx.utils.config.Config`.

    The checkpoint is the last artifact whose name contains ``prefix``, or, with
    ``iterations``, the first one written at or past that many training steps.
    Returns the checkpoint's directory.
    """
    run_dir = Path(run_dir)
    api = wandb.Api()
    run = api.run(f'{entity}/{project}/{run_id}')

    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        config_artifact = get_latest_artifact(run, 'config')
    except ValueError:
        save_config(unflatten_config(run.config), run_dir / 'config.yaml')
    else:
        config_artifact.download(root=run_dir)

    policy_artifact = (
        get_latest_artifact(run, prefix) if iterations is None
        else get_earliest_artifact(run, prefix, iterations)
    )
    artifact_dir = policy_artifact.download(
        root=str(run_dir / str(policy_artifact.metadata['iteration']))
    )
    return artifact_dir

class MujocoPlotter:
    """Collects MuJoCo mjData fields over time and exports to HDF5."""

    DEFAULT_PLOTKEY: list[str] = ['qpos', 'qvel', 'ctrl', 'sensordata', 'qfrc_actuator']

    def __init__(self, plotkey: list[str] | None = None, record_time: bool = True) -> None:
        self.plotkey: list[str] = plotkey if plotkey is not None else self.DEFAULT_PLOTKEY
        self.record_time: bool = record_time
        self.data: dict[str, list[Any]] = {key: [] for key in self.plotkey}
        if record_time:
            self.data['time'] = []

    def add_row(self, data: mujoco.MjData) -> None:
        """Append one timestep of data from an mjData-like object."""
        if self.record_time:
            self.data['time'].append(getattr(data, 'time'))
        for key in self.plotkey:
            self.data[key].append(getattr(data, key).copy())

    def to_numpy(self) -> None:
        """Convert all stored lists to numpy arrays in-place."""
        for key in self.plotkey:
            self.data[key] = np.array(self.data[key])

    def save_to_h5(self, filename: str | Path) -> None:
        """Write all data to an HDF5 file."""
        with h5py.File(filename, 'w') as f:
            for key in self.data:
                f.create_dataset(key, data=np.array(self.data[key]))

    @classmethod
    def time_idx(cls, time: float, data: dict[str, list[Any]]) -> int:
        """Return the index of the last entry at or before *time*."""
        if 'time' not in data:
            raise ValueError("Time data is required for indexing.")
        time_array = np.array(data['time'])
        idx = np.searchsorted(time_array, time)
        if idx == 0 or idx == len(time_array):
            raise ValueError("Time index out of bounds.")
        return idx - 1

class RewardPlotter:
    """Accumulates per-step reward components and produces a summary figure."""

    def __init__(self, metrics: Sequence[str]) -> None:
        self.axkey: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.axdata: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
        self.rewards: list[float] = []
        for i, metric in enumerate(metrics):
            self.axkey[metric] = i
            self.axdata[metric] = []

    def add_row(self, metrics: dict[str, float], reward: float) -> None:
        """Record one timestep of metric values and total reward."""
        self.rewards.append(reward)
        for metric in metrics:
            self.axdata[metric].append(metrics[metric])

    def plot(self, figsize: tuple[int, int] = (10, 10),
             title: str = 'Metrics') -> tuple[mfig.Figure, np.ndarray]:
        """Create a multi-subplot figure of all metrics plus total reward."""
        nrows, ncols = get_subplot_grid(len(self.axdata) + 1)
        fig, axs = plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=figsize)
        axs = axs.flatten()
        fig.suptitle(title)

        for metric in self.axdata:
            axs[self.axkey[metric]].set_title(metric)
            axs[self.axkey[metric]].plot(self.axdata[metric])

        axs[len(self.axdata)].set_title('Total Reward')
        axs[len(self.axdata)].plot(self.rewards)
        return fig, axs

class Progress:
    """Brax PPO progress callback that accumulates the eval reward curve.

    Pass :meth:`plot_progress` as brax's ``progress_fn``. The curve is rewritten to
    ``save_dir/progress.csv`` on every eval, and every scalar metric is logged to
    ``run`` (e.g. a wandb run) when one is given.
    """

    def __init__(self, save_dir, total_timesteps=None, run=None) -> None:
        self.run                = run
        self.times              = []
        self.x_data             = []
        self.y_data             = []
        self.y_dataerr          = []
        self.save_dir           = Path(save_dir)
        self.total_timesteps    = total_timesteps

    def load(self, before=None) -> None:
        """Refill the curves from an earlier job's ``progress.csv`` (see :func:`load_progress`)."""
        load_progress(
            self.save_dir, self.times, self.x_data, self.y_data, self.y_dataerr,
            before=before,
        )

    def plot_progress(self, num_steps, metrics) -> None:
        """Brax PPO progress callback: accumulate eval reward, log native W&B lines.

        Logs every scalar brax metric via ``run.log`` so each renders as a native,
        interactive W&B line chart, and writes the raw curve to ``progress.csv``.
        """
        print('=== TRAINING EPOCH ===')
        print('time', datetime.now(ZoneInfo("America/New_York")).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"))
        print('num_steps', num_steps)
        if self.total_timesteps is not None:
            print('total steps', self.total_timesteps)

        self.times.append(datetime.now())
        self.x_data.append(int(num_steps))
        self.y_data.append(float(metrics["eval/episode_reward"]))
        self.y_dataerr.append(float(metrics["eval/episode_reward_std"]))
        pd.DataFrame(
            {
                'times': self.times,
                'x': self.x_data,
                'y': self.y_data,
                'yerr': self.y_dataerr
            }
        ).to_csv(
            self.save_dir / 'progress.csv',
            index=False
        )

        if np.isnan(self.y_data[-1]) or np.isnan(self.y_dataerr[-1]):
            raise Exception(f'NaN found... \n\n{self.y_data}\n\n{self.y_dataerr}')

        if self.run:
            # Log every scalar brax metric so each gets a native line chart.
            scalars = {}
            for k, v in metrics.items():
                try:
                    scalars[k] = float(v)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    continue
            self.run.log(scalars, step=num_steps)

def load_progress(save_dir, times, x_data, y_data, y_dataerr, before=None) -> None:
    """Refill a :class:`Progress`'s curves from the `progress.csv` a previous job wrote.

    The callback rewrites the file from these lists on every eval, so a continued run
    that started them empty would drop the epochs it inherited. `before` is the step it
    restarts from: rows at or past it are left out, the run evaluating that state again
    as its own first row.
    """
    path = Path(save_dir) / 'progress.csv'
    if not path.exists():
        return
    frame = pd.read_csv(path)
    if before is not None:
        frame = frame[frame['x'] < before]
    times.extend(pd.to_datetime(frame['times']).tolist())
    x_data.extend(frame['x'].tolist())
    y_data.extend(frame['y'].tolist())
    y_dataerr.extend(frame['yerr'].tolist())

def add_ICD_config():
    """
    Attempt to write an NVIDIA ICD config for libglvnd (Linux only).
    This file typically requires root privileges. We try to create it only on Linux
    and catch permission errors — if we can't write it, just warn.
    """
    if platform.system() != "Linux":
        return

    NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH = "/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/10_nvidia.json"
    if os.path.exists(NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH):
        logger.debug(f"ICD config already exists at {NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH}.")
        return

    icd_json = """{
  "file_format_version" : "1.0.0",
  "ICD" : {
    "library_path" : "libEGL_nvidia.so.0"
  }
}
"""
    try:
        # Attempt to create directories if missing
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH), exist_ok=True)
        with open(NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH, "w") as f:
            f.write(icd_json)
        logger.debug(f"Wrote NVIDIA ICD config to {NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH}.")
    except PermissionError:
        logger.debug(f"Permission denied: cannot write {NVIDIA_ICD_CONFIG_PATH}. Run as root to install ICD, or skip this step.")
    except Exception as e:
        logger.debug(f"Unexpected error writing ICD config: {e}")

def check_gpu_connection():
    """
    Lightweight GPU presence check: return True if NVIDIA tools are available and responding.
    Don't call this on macOS (no nvidia-smi there).
    """
    if platform.system() != "Linux":
        logger.debug("Skipping NVIDIA connectivity check (non-Linux system).")
        return False

    nvidia_smi_path = shutil.which("nvidia-smi")
    if not nvidia_smi_path:
        logger.debug("nvidia-smi not found on PATH.")
        return False

    try:
        subprocess.run([nvidia_smi_path], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        logger.debug("NVIDIA GPU appears available.")
        return True
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        logger.debug("nvidia-smi returned non-zero exit code — GPU may be unreachable or driver issue.")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        logger.debug(f"Error checking nvidia-smi: {e}")
        return False

def delete_failed_runs(entity: str, project: str, assume_yes: bool = False) -> None:
    """Finds and deletes all failed/crashed runs in a specified W&B project,

    printing the number of associated logged artifacts for each run. Each
    deletion is confirmed interactively unless ``assume_yes`` is set.
    """
    # Initialize the public API
    api = wandb.Api()

    path = f"{entity}/{project}"
    print(f"Fetching runs from: {path}...")

    try:
        # Retrieve all runs for the project path
        runs = api.runs(path)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error connecting to project path '{path}': {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return

    deleted_count = 0
    skipped_count = 0

    for run in runs:
        # Filter for failed or crashed states
        if run.state in ["failed", "crashed"]:
            try:
                # Retrieve and count the logged artifacts for this run
                logged_artifacts = list(run.logged_artifacts())
                artifact_count = len(logged_artifacts)
            except Exception:
                artifact_count = 0

            print(f"Run: {run.name} ({run.id})")
            print(f"  - State: {run.state}")
            print(f"  - Logged Artifacts: {artifact_count}")

            if not assume_yes and not _confirm(
                f"Delete this run and its {artifact_count} artifact(s)?"
            ):
                print("  - Skipped.")
                print("-" * 40)
                skipped_count += 1
                continue

            print("  - Deleting...")
            print("-" * 40)

            # Deletes the run and all of its associated artifacts
            run.delete(delete_artifacts=True)
            deleted_count += 1

    print(
        f"\nExecution finished. Successfully deleted {deleted_count} runs "
        f"({skipped_count} skipped)."
    )

example/ holds a complete task built on DeepMind Control's Cheetah. Its two scripts cover the whole workflow:

Script What it does Walkthrough example/train.py Trains a PPO policy, checkpoints it, and saves a video of the result Training a policy example/rollout.py Loads a checkpoint (or a dummy zero/random policy), rolls it out, and saves a video and reward plot Rolling out a policy

They share these supporting files:

File Purpose cheetah.xml The MuJoCo model cheetah.py Cheetah(SwappableBase): reset, step, observations, rewards, termination. See Writing an environment. cheetah.yaml The run config: name, save directory, backend, env_config, learning_params. See The config file. create_environment.py Maps the config's env name to an environment class cheetah_model_input.py A lean Cheetah that takes the mjx.Model as an argument, so many model variants can be vmapped

Run every script from the repository root as a module (python -m example.train ...), so that from example.create_environment import ... resolves.

docs.title: Rolling out a policy
docs.text:
example/rollout.py loads a trained policy, runs it in the environment, and saves a video and a plot of every reward term. It can also drive the environment with zero or random actions, which is the quickest way to check a new environment before training anything.

python -m example.rollout --config example/cheetah.yaml                       # latest checkpoint
python -m example.rollout --config example/cheetah.yaml --inference_fn zero   # no policy, zero actions
python -m example.rollout --config example/results/cheetah/test/config.yaml \
    --model_path example/results/cheetah/test/000025016320                     # a specific checkpoint

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --config (required) Path to the run's YAML config --inference_fn policy policy loads a trained checkpoint; zero or random send dummy actions instead --model_path latest A checkpoint directory to load instead of the newest one in the run directory --T 10.0 Rollout length in seconds --width, --height 640, 480 Video size in pixels --camera track Camera to render from --stochastic off Sample actions from the policy instead of taking the mean action --seed none Seed NumPy's random generator, which picks the initial state's random key, so rollouts repeat

docs.title: 1. Set up rendering and keep JAX on the CPU
docs.text:
os.environ["MUJOCO_GL"] = "egl"
os.environ['JAX_PLATFORMS'] = 'cpu'

egl renders without a display. JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu keeps JAX off the GPU: the rollout steps a single environment, usually on the NumPy backend, so the only JAX work is evaluating the small policy network, which is fast on the CPU.

docs.title: 2. Read the config and build the environment
docs.text:
cfg = mm.Config(config_path)
env, env_params = create_environment(cfg)

Unlike training, this builds the environment on the backend the config names. The example config uses backend: np, which steps the C MuJoCo bindings directly. That is fast for a single environment, and you can set breakpoints and print values inside reset and step, which JAX's tracing does not allow.

Check your environment is JAX-compatible

Training always uses jnp. Before training a new environment, run this script once with backend: jnp in the config and --inference_fn zero. Code that works on NumPy but not under JAX (Python if on array values, in-place array writes) fails here quickly, instead of after you have queued a training job.

To roll out an older run, pass the config.yaml saved in that run's directory. Its save_dir and name point back at the same run, and its git_hash records the commit the policy was trained at.

docs.title: 3. Build the inference function
docs.text:
if inference_fn_type == 'policy':
    inference_fn = mm.learning.inference.load_policy(
        cfg.run_dir,
        deterministic   = deterministic,
        checkpoint_path = model_path
    )
    inference_fn = jax.jit(inference_fn)
else:
    inference_fn = mm.make_dummy_inference_fn(env=env, mode=inference_fn_type)

An inference function maps (obs, rng) to (action, extras), the same signature Brax uses.

  • load_policy restores a checkpoint: the one at checkpoint_path if given, otherwise the newest step directory in run_dir (found with get_last_model). Each checkpoint carries its network config, so nothing about the architecture has to match the current YAML. deterministic=True takes the mean action. The result is jitted so each call is a single compiled function.
  • make_dummy_inference_fn returns a policy that sends all zeros (zero) or uniform random actions in [-1, 1] (random).

docs.title: 4. Roll out
docs.text:
frames, _, reward_plotter, _, _ = mm.eval.rollout_policy(
    inference_fn = inference_fn,
    env          = env,
    n_steps      = int(T / env.dt),
    camera       = camera,
    width        = width,
    height       = height
)

rollout_policy:

  1. Gets step and reset functions from get_step_reset, jitted on the jnp backend and plain Python on np.
  2. Resets the environment with a random key drawn from NumPy (which is why --seed makes rollouts repeat).
  3. Steps n_steps times, or until the environment reports done. Each step it records MuJoCo data (qpos, qvel, ctrl, ...) in a MujocoPlotter, reward terms in a RewardPlotter, and chosen info fields in an InfoPlotter.
  4. Renders every state to a frame.

It returns (frames, trajectory, reward_plotter, data_plotter, info_plotter). This script keeps the frames and the reward plotter. The other three are there for your own analysis: the plotters can write their data to HDF5 with save_to_h5.

docs.title: 5. Save the video and reward plot
docs.text:
mm.utils.plotting.save_video(frames, env.dt, Path(f'example/videos/{cfg.env_name}-rollout.mp4'))
mm.utils.plotting.save_metrics(reward_plotter, Path(f'example/plots/{cfg.env_name}-reward.pdf'))

save_video writes the frames at the control rate (1 / env.dt frames per second), so the video plays in real time. save_metrics plots each weighted reward term and the total reward over the rollout, one subplot each.

Note

If example/videos/ or example/plots/ does not exist, both functions ask on the terminal whether to create it, and skip saving if you answer no.

example/rollout.py 
import os
os.environ["MUJOCO_GL"] = "egl"
os.environ['JAX_PLATFORMS']='cpu'
import numpy as np
import minimal_mjx as mm
from pathlib import Path
from example.create_environment import create_environment
import jax
import argparse

def main(
    config_path      : Path,
    inference_fn_type: str = 'policy',
    model_path       : Path = None,
    T                : float = 10.0,
    width            : int = None,
    height           : int = None,
    camera           : str = 'track',
    deterministic    : bool = True,
    seed             : int = None
):
    if seed is not None:
        np.random.seed(seed)

    cfg = mm.Config(config_path)
    env, env_params = create_environment(cfg)

    if inference_fn_type == 'policy':
        inference_fn = mm.learning.inference.load_policy(
            cfg.run_dir,
            deterministic   = deterministic,
            checkpoint_path = model_path
        )
        inference_fn = jax.jit(inference_fn)
    else:
        inference_fn = mm.make_dummy_inference_fn(
            env  = env,
            mode = inference_fn_type
        )

    frames, _, reward_plotter, _, _ = mm.eval.rollout_policy(
        inference_fn    = inference_fn,
        env             = env,
        n_steps         = int(T / env.dt),
        camera          = camera,
        width           = width,
        height          = height
    )

    mm.utils.plotting.save_video(
        frames,
        env.dt,
        Path(f'example/videos/{cfg.env_name}-rollout.mp4')
    )

    mm.utils.plotting.save_metrics(
        reward_plotter,
        Path(f'example/plots/{cfg.env_name}-reward.pdf')
    )

if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Roll out a policy and save a video and reward plot.')
    parser.add_argument('--config', type=Path, required=True, help='Path to the config file')
    parser.add_argument('--inference_fn', default='policy', choices=['policy', 'zero', 'random'],
                        help='Use the trained policy, or a dummy zero/random action function')
    parser.add_argument('--model_path', type=Path, default=None,
                        help='Checkpoint to load (defaults to the latest checkpoint in the run dir)')
    parser.add_argument('--T', type=float, default=10.0, help='Rollout duration in seconds')
    parser.add_argument('--width', type=int, default=640, help='Video width in pixels')
    parser.add_argument('--height', type=int, default=480, help='Video height in pixels')
    parser.add_argument('--camera', default='track', help='Camera name to render from')
    parser.add_argument('--stochastic', action='store_true', help='Sample actions instead of using the mean')
    parser.add_argument('--seed', type=int, default=None, help='Random seed for the initial state')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    main(
        config_path       = args.config,
        inference_fn_type = args.inference_fn,
        model_path        = args.model_path,
        T                 = args.T,

docs.title: Training a policy
docs.text:
example/train.py trains a PPO policy for the Cheetah, checkpoints it as it goes, and saves a video of the trained policy at the end. This page walks through the script step by step, then shows what a finished run looks like on disk.

python -m example.train --config example/cheetah.yaml             # logs to Weights & Biases
python -m example.train --config example/cheetah.yaml --no_wandb  # no W&B

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --config (required) Path to the run's YAML config --no_wandb off Turn off Weights & Biases logging --wandb_entity njanwani-gatech W&B entity (user or team) to log to --wandb_project my-awesome-project-2 W&B project to log to --T 10.0 Seconds of the trained policy to save as a video. 0 skips the video. --camera track Camera to render the video from

docs.title: 1. Pick a rendering backend
docs.text:
import os
os.environ["MUJOCO_GL"] = "egl"

MuJoCo reads MUJOCO_GL when it is first imported, so it is set before anything else. egl renders on the GPU without a display, which is what you want on a cluster. The video in step 7 is the only rendering the script does. See setup_gpu if you want this picked automatically per machine.

docs.title: 2. Read the config
docs.text:
cfg = mm.utils.Config(config_path)

Config loads the YAML file and exposes the values the library needs as properties: cfg.env_name, cfg.env_params, cfg.ppo_params, cfg.network_params, cfg.run_dir, and so on. It is the only code that knows the YAML layout. Every library function takes plain arguments, so you can subclass Config for a different layout or skip it. See The config file.

docs.title: 3. Build the environment
docs.text:
env, env_params = create_environment(cfg, for_training=True)

create_environment (in example/create_environment.py) maps cfg.env_name to an environment class, here Cheetah. for_training=True forces the jnp (JAX/MJX) backend whatever the config says, because Brax trains thousands of environments in parallel on the accelerator and needs every step to be traceable by JAX.

docs.title: 4. Create the run directory and save the config
docs.text:
run_dir = mm.create_training_directory(cfg.run_dir, overwrite=cfg.is_test)
cfg.save(run_dir / 'config.yaml', make_dir=False)

create_training_directory creates save_dir/name (here example/results/cheetah/test). It refuses to reuse a directory that already holds training output, unless overwrite is set. Runs named test set it, so you can rerun a scratch config freely; any other name protects its earlier results.

Config.save then writes the config next to the checkpoints. For runs not named test it also records the current git commit as git_hash, and asks you to confirm if the working tree has uncommitted changes. That saved config.yaml is what you later pass to rollout.py to reproduce this run.

docs.title: 5. Start a Weights & Biases run (optional)
docs.text:
run = mm.initialize_wandb(
    name    = str(run_dir).replace('/', ''),
    entity  = wandb_entity,
    project = wandb_project,
    config  = cfg.cfg.to_dict()
)

initialize_wandb wraps wandb.init and logs the whole config, nested as in the YAML file. With --no_wandb, run is None and every later step skips its W&B logging.

docs.title: 6. Train
docs.text:
make_inference_fn, params, _ = mm.train(
    env            = env,
    eval_env       = env,
    run_dir        = run_dir,
    handle_params  = mm.setup_ppo,
    ppo_params     = cfg.ppo_params,
    network_params = cfg.network_params,
    run            = run,
    overwrite      = cfg.is_test,
)

train does the heavy lifting:

  1. Prepares the run directory and records the W&B run id in wandb_run_id.txt, so a later job can continue the same W&B run.
  2. Builds the trainer by calling handle_params(ppo_params, network_params, resumed). setup_ppo returns Brax's PPO trainer with your ppo_params bound, and a factory for the policy and value networks built from network_params. To use another algorithm, pass your own handler with the same signature.
  3. Attaches two callbacks that Brax calls after every evaluation (num_evals times over the run):
    • a progress callback, by default Progress, which appends the evaluation reward to progress.csv, logs every scalar metric to W&B, and stops training if the reward becomes NaN;
    • a checkpoint callback, which writes the policy parameters with save_model into a directory named after the step count (and uploads it as a W&B artifact).
  4. Runs Brax PPO, wrapping the environment with MuJoCo Playground's wrap_for_brax_training, then prints the time spent compiling and the time spent training.

It returns make_inference_fn, the trained params, and Brax's final metrics.

Continuing a run

mm.train(..., resume=True) continues from the newest checkpoint in run_dir instead of refusing to touch it. num_timesteps is then the run's total budget, and training covers only the steps still owed. To train longer, raise num_timesteps in the saved config and resume.

docs.title: 7. Save a video of the trained policy
docs.text:
inference_fn = jax.jit(make_inference_fn(params, deterministic=True))
frames, *_ = mm.rollout_policy(
    inference_fn = inference_fn,
    env          = env,
    n_steps      = int(T / env.dt),
    camera       = camera,
    width        = 640,
    height       = 480
)
video_path = run_dir / 'rollout.mp4'
mm.save_video(frames, env.dt, video_path)
if run is not None:
    run.log({'rollout': wandb.Video(str(video_path), format='mp4')})

make_inference_fn(params, deterministic=True) builds a policy that always takes the mean action rather than sampling. rollout_policy runs it for T seconds and renders the frames, and save_video writes them to run_dir/rollout.mp4 at the control rate. The video is also logged to W&B.

This uses the training environment (jnp backend) rather than building a separate np one. Rolling out a policy shows the more flexible way to evaluate a checkpoint after training.

docs.title: What a finished run looks like
docs.text:
The example run in example/results/cheetah/test trained for 50M environment steps with 128 parallel environments and 15 evaluations:

example/results/cheetah/test/
├── config.yaml          # the config this run used (pass it to rollout.py)
├── progress.csv         # one row per evaluation: time, step, reward, reward std
├── rollout.mp4          # step 7's video of the final policy
├── wandb_run_id.txt     # the W&B run this directory belongs to
├── 000000000000/        # one checkpoint per evaluation, named by env step
├── 000003573760/
├── ...
└── 000050032640/        # newest checkpoint; rollout.py loads this one by default
    ├── ppo_network_config.json
    └── ...              # Orbax checkpoint files

Checkpoints land every 3,573,760 steps: Brax rounds the evaluation interval up to a whole number of training iterations (batch_size × unroll_length × num_minibatches = 2,560 environment steps here), which is also why the last one sits slightly past 50M. Each checkpoint directory holds everything needed to rebuild the policy, including its ppo_network_config.json (observation and action sizes, layer sizes, activation).

progress.csv gives the learning curve. Brax evaluates once before training starts, so the first row is the untrained policy. In this run the gap between the first two evaluations was about 70 seconds, mostly JAX compiling the training step (train prints it as time to jit). After that, evaluations came every 31 seconds or so, and the run took about 8 minutes in all:

And rollout.mp4 shows the final policy:

docs.title: Full script
docs.text:
example/train.py 
import os
os.environ["MUJOCO_GL"] = "egl"
import minimal_mjx as mm
from pathlib import Path
from example.create_environment import create_environment
import argparse
import jax
import wandb

def main(
    config_path  : Path,
    use_wandb    : bool = True,
    wandb_entity : str = 'njanwani-gatech',
    wandb_project: str = 'my-awesome-project-2',
    T            : float = 10.0,
    camera       : str = 'track'
):
    # Read configuration file
    cfg = mm.utils.Config(config_path)

    # Create environment
    env, env_params = create_environment(cfg, for_training=True)

    # Create the run directory and save the config next to the checkpoints
    # (runs named 'test' may be overwritten and skip recording the git hash)
    run_dir = mm.create_training_directory(cfg.run_dir, overwrite=cfg.is_test)
    cfg.save(run_dir / 'config.yaml', make_dir=False)

    # Initialize Weights and Biases Run object (if you want to use it)
    if not use_wandb:
        run = None
    else:
        run = mm.initialize_wandb(
            name    = str(run_dir).replace('/', ''),
            entity  = wandb_entity,
            project = wandb_project,
            config  = cfg.cfg.to_dict()
        )

    # Begin training
    make_inference_fn, params, _ = mm.train(
        env                       = env,
        eval_env                  = env,
        run_dir                   = run_dir,
        handle_params             = mm.setup_ppo,
        train_fn_params           = cfg.ppo_params,
        network_factory_params    = cfg.network_params,
        run                       = run,
        overwrite                 = cfg.is_test,
        progress_cls              = mm.Progress
    )

    # Save a video of the trained policy
    if T > 0:
        inference_fn = jax.jit(make_inference_fn(params, deterministic=True))
        frames, *_ = mm.rollout_policy(
            inference_fn = inference_fn,
            env          = env,
            n_steps      = int(T / env.dt),
            camera       = camera,
            width        = 640,
            height       = 480
        )
        video_path = run_dir / 'rollout.mp4'
        mm.save_video(frames, env.dt, video_path)
        if run is not None:
            run.log({'rollout': wandb.Video(str(video_path), format='mp4')})

if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Train a policy from a config file.')
    parser.add_argument('--config', type=Path, required=True, help='Path to the config file')
    parser.add_argument('--no_wandb', action='store_true', help='Disable Weights and Biases logging')
    parser.add_argument('--wandb_entity', default='njanwani-gatech', help='Weights and Biases entity')
    parser.add_argument('--wandb_project', default='my-awesome-project-2', help='Weights and Biases project')
    parser.add_argument('--T', type=float, default=10.0,
                        help='Seconds of the trained policy to save as a video (0 to skip)')
    parser.add_argument('--camera', default='track', help='Camera name to render the video from')
    args = parser.parse_args()

    main(
        config_path   = args.config,
        use_wandb     = not args.no_wandb,
        wandb_entity  = args.wandb_entity,
        wandb_project = args.wandb_project,
        T             = args.T,
        camera        = args.camera
    )

docs.title: The config file
docs.text:
Every run is described by one YAML file. The example scripts read it through Config, which turns its sections into the plain arguments the library functions take. Here is example/cheetah.yaml:

name: test
save_dir: example/results/cheetah
description: ""
algorithm: ppo
env: Cheetah
backend: np # jnp or np. Always uses jnp for training
env_config:
  ctrl_dt: 0.01
  sim_dt: 0.01
  action_scale: 1.0
  history_length: 5
  ideal_base_height: 0.5
  ideal_base_vel: 0.5
  min_base_height: 0.3
  add_random_joint_state: False
  add_random_pitch: False
  reward:
    weights: 
      run:        1.0
      height:     10.0
      energy:     1.0
      alive:      1.0
      done:       0
  termination:
    enabled: true        # Enable or disable early termination
    base_height: 0.2
learning_params:
  ppo_params:
    action_repeat: 1
    batch_size: 64
    clipping_epsilon: 0.1
    deterministic_eval: true
    discounting: 0.98
    entropy_cost: 0.01
    episode_length: 500
    learning_rate: 0.0005
    max_grad_norm: 1.0
    normalize_observations: true
    num_envs: 128
    num_evals: 15
    num_minibatches: 2
    num_timesteps: 50000000
    num_updates_per_batch: 4
    reward_scaling: 1.0
    unroll_length: 20
  network_params:
    policy_hidden_layer_sizes: [64, 64]
    value_hidden_layer_sizes:  [64, 64]

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text:
Key Read as Meaning name cfg.name Run name. The run directory is save_dir/name. A run named test may be overwritten and does not record a git hash. save_dir cfg.save_dir Parent directory for all runs made from this config description Free text for your own notes algorithm cfg.algorithm Training algorithm; defaults to ppo env cfg.env_name Environment class name, which create_environment maps to a class backend cfg.backend np or jnp for rollouts. Training always uses jnp. git_hash Not in your config: Config.save adds it to the copy saved in the run directory

cfg.run_dir combines save_dir and name, so example/cheetah.yaml trains into example/results/cheetah/test/.

docs.title: env_config
docs.text:
Everything under env_config is handed to the environment as env_params (cfg.env_params), and the environment reads it as self.params. The library itself reads only these keys:

Key Meaning ctrl_dt Control period in seconds: how often the policy acts. This is env.dt. sim_dt Physics timestep. Each step runs ctrl_dt / sim_dt physics substeps. reward.weights One weight per reward term. The keys must match the names your reward_function returns.

Any other key is yours to define and read in your environment. Cheetah reads action_scale in step; the remaining keys in the example (history_length, ideal_base_height, termination, ...) show the kind of settings an environment might take, but Cheetah does not use them.

The config is locked

MuJoCo Playground locks env_params when the environment is built. Reading a key that is missing from the YAML raises an error, so add every key your environment reads to the config.

docs.title: learning_params
docs.text:
Section Read as Meaning ppo_params cfg.ppo_params Passed as keyword arguments to Brax's PPO train function. See the Brax PPO docs for every option. network_params cfg.network_params Passed to Brax's make_ppo_networks, for example the hidden layer sizes

A few PPO settings worth knowing:

  • num_timesteps: total environment steps for the run. When resuming, this is the total budget, not the steps still to go.
  • num_envs: environments simulated in parallel.
  • num_evals: how many times training pauses to evaluate the policy. Each evaluation also writes a checkpoint and a row of progress.csv.
  • episode_length: steps per episode before the environment is reset.
  • normalize_observations: keep a running mean and variance of observations. The normalizer is saved inside each checkpoint.

docs.title: Using your own layout
docs.text:
Library functions never read the YAML directly. To use a different layout, subclass Config and override the properties that differ:

class MyConfig(mm.Config):
    @property
    def ppo_params(self) -> dict:
        return self.cfg.training.ppo.to_dict()

Or skip Config and pass run_dir, ppo_params and network_params to train yourself.

docs.title: Writing an environment
docs.text:
An environment subclasses SwappableBase. You write it once, and it runs on either backend:

  • jnp uses JAX and MJX. Brax trains thousands of copies in parallel on the accelerator, so training always uses this backend.
  • np uses NumPy and MuJoCo's C bindings. It is fast for a single environment, and ordinary Python debugging works: breakpoints, prints, if statements on values.

This page walks through example/cheetah.py to show what you need to implement.

docs.title: Backend handles
docs.text:
The trick that makes one class run on both backends: never call np, jnp, mjx or jax.random directly. SwappableBase sets up handles that point at the right one:

Handle jnp backend np backend self._np jax.numpy numpy self._step_fn(data, ctrl) mjx_env.step, with the configured substeps mj_step on a copy of data self._data_init_fn(qpos, qvel, ctrl, time, xfrc_applied) mjx.make_data + mjx.forward MjData + mj_forward self._state_init_fn(data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info) mjx_env.State EnvState self._split(rng, n) jax.random.split yields None self._uniform, self._normal jax.random np.random self._set_val_fn(arr, val, min_idx, max_idx) arr.at[...].set(val) copy, then assign self._cond(pred, true_fn, false_fn, x) jax.lax.cond Python if

docs.title: __init__
docs.text:
Pass the MuJoCo XML, the env_params from the config, and the backend:

class Cheetah(mm.envs.SwappableBase):
    def __init__(self, env_params, backend):
        super().__init__(
            xml_path   = CheetahInterface.XML,
            env_params = env_params,
            backend    = backend,
        )

SwappableBase compiles the model, sets its timestep to env_config.sim_dt, and builds the backend handles. num_free (default 3) is the number of qpos entries taken by the floating base; the Cheetah's are rootx, rootz and rooty.

docs.title: reset(rng)
docs.text:
Build the initial data, compute the first observation and rewards, and return a state:

def reset(self, rng):
    rng, qpos_key, qvel_key = self._split(rng, 3)
    qpos = self._np.hstack([CheetahInterface.DEFAULT_FF, CheetahInterface.DEFAULT_JT])
    ...
    data = self._data_init_fn(qpos=qpos, qvel=qvel, ctrl=ctrl, time=0.0,
                              xfrc_applied=self._np.zeros((self._mj_model.nbody, 6)))
    info = {'xposbefore': 0.0, 'xposafter': 0.01, 'ang': 0.0}
    rewards = self.reward_function(data=data, action=ctrl, info=info, done=False)
    reward, metrics = self.get_reward_and_metrics(rewards, {})
    obs = self._get_obs(data, info)
    return self._state_init_fn(data, obs, reward, done, metrics, info)

Under JAX, every key in info and metrics must already exist after reset, because the state's structure cannot change between steps. Initialize anything step will write here.

docs.title: step(state, action)
docs.text:
Apply the action, advance the physics, and return the next state:

def step(self, state, action):
    state.info['xposbefore'] = state.data.qpos[0]
    action = self._np.clip(self.params.action_scale * action, -1.0, 1.0)
    data = self._step_fn(state.data, action)
    state.info['xposafter'] = data.qpos[0]
    state.info['ang']       = data.qpos[2]

    done = self.fall_termination(state.info)
    rewards = self.reward_function(data=data, action=action, info=state.info, done=done)
    reward, metrics = self.get_reward_and_metrics(rewards, state.metrics)
    obs = self._get_obs(data, state.info)
    return self._state_init_fn(data, obs, reward, done.astype(float), metrics, state.info)

Use state.info to carry values from one step to the next, as the Cheetah does with its x position to compute forward velocity.

docs.title: reward_function(data, action, info, done)
docs.text:
Return a dict of named reward terms:

def reward_function(self, data, action, info, done):
    return {
        'alive'  : self.reward_alive(),
        'energy' : self.reward_energy(action),
        'height' : self.reward_height(data),
        'run'    : self.reward_run(info),
        'done'   : self.reward_done(done),
    }

get_reward_and_metrics multiplies each term by env_config.reward.weights[name] and sums them into the scalar reward. It also logs each weighted term as reward/<name> in metrics, which is what appears in W&B and in the rollout reward plot. Every name you return needs a weight in the config; set a weight to 0 to log a term without rewarding it.

SwappableBase provides some common terms: reward_alive, reward_action_rate, reward_euclidean_imitation, reward_vector_size and exp_reward.

docs.title: _get_obs(data, info) and action_size
docs.text:
def _get_obs(self, data, info):
    obs = self._np.concatenate([data.qpos[1:], self._np.clip(data.qvel, -10.0, 10.0)])
    return {'state': obs, 'privileged_state': obs}

@property
def action_size(self):
    return 6

Returning a dict lets the policy and the value function see different inputs. By default both read obs['state']. To give the critic information the robot would not have at deployment (asymmetric actor-critic), put it in privileged_state and set value_obs_key: privileged_state under network_params in the config.

For observations that need recent history, SwappableBase has make_history and update_history.

docs.title: Registering the environment
docs.text:
The example scripts find environments by name through example/create_environment.py. Add a case for yours:

match cfg.env_name:
    case 'Cheetah':
        from example.cheetah import Cheetah
        env = Cheetah(**common_kwargs, **env_kwargs)
    case 'MyRobot':
        from example.my_robot import MyRobot
        env = MyRobot(**common_kwargs, **env_kwargs)

Then set env: MyRobot in your config, and check it with a zero-action rollout on both backends before training (see Rolling out a policy).
